channel.title: Wombat
channel.description: New versions of Wombat, the Markdown viewer for Mac.

item.title: Wombat 0.5.2
item.description:
### Added
- Settings has a Default App section that says which app opens Markdown files. Unless that's Wombat, a button, Make Wombat the Default, makes Wombat the default for every Markdown extension it knows (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd`, `.mkdn`, `.mdwn`, `.mdtxt`, `.mdtext` and `.mdx`), while plain text files stay with the app that opens them. Settings checks again when its window comes forward and when you switch back to Wombat, so a change made in Finder shows up. If the change fails, or macOS accepts it but still wouldn't open Markdown files in Wombat, a short alert gives Finder's steps instead. The Mac App Store version shows those steps (File › Get Info, Open with, Change All) in place of the button, because the App Sandbox keeps apps from changing the default app. README, the support page and the tester notes put the Settings button first and Finder's way second.

item.title: Wombat 0.5.1
item.description:
### Added - File › Save… (⌘S) saves Markdown you pasted (File › New from Clipboard, ⌘V or a drop) as a `.md` file. The save panel suggests the pasted document's title as the name, with slashes and colons replaced and without a `.md` of its own, and the file holds the text exactly as pasted, line endings included. The window then shows that file like one you opened: its name in the title bar, links and images next to it, reloading when it changes, and in Open Recent. In the Mac App Store version, the folder access bar asks for its folder when images there need it. Save… is only for pasted text: Wombat still never changes a file it opened, won't save over a file a window shows or a link to one, and closes unsaved pasted text without asking. The support page says so. ### Changed - A pasted document is titled after the title in its front matter, or else its first heading or line of text without Markdown or HTML markup, passing over logos, badges, code and tables. A pasted README that starts with a centered logo is titled by its heading rather than `

`, and front matter no longer gives `---`. - The privacy policy says pasted text is written to disk only when you save it with File › Save…, where you choose in the save panel. It used to say Wombat never writes pasted text to disk.

item.title: Wombat 0.5.0
item.description:
### Added
- Wombat keeps itself up to date. The download checks for a new version once a day, downloads it in the background and installs it when you quit Wombat, so it's there the next time you open it. Wombat › Check for Updates… checks at once, and Settings › Check for updates automatically turns the daily checks off. Each update must carry Wombat's signature before it's unpacked. Copies of 0.4.0 can't update themselves: replace that one by hand. The Mac App Store version has no updater, since the App Store updates it. - The Help menu opens Wombat's website, the support page and the privacy policy.
### Changed
- The privacy policy says what an update check sends: your IP address to GitHub, which hosts the feed, and Wombat's and the updater's versions, with no profile of your Mac. It also says how to turn checks off and that the App Store version doesn't check, and its list of what to delete to remove Wombat's data includes the folder where macOS keeps Wombat's network data. The support page explains how each version updates.
